title: Characterize and route the measured DPMI AX=0501 memory allocation frontier
description: W2-047 original-byte replay now resumes after INT 2Fh AX=1500 and continues through a successful extra AX=0100 DOS block allocation. The guest then enters DPMI AX=0501 linear memory allocation repeatedly; the current host returns dpmi31.allocate_memory.unavailable and the bounded replay reaches one million instructions without a later explicit unsupported trap. Capture the exact first AX=0501 call (size, guest EIP, allocator state, failure reason), distinguish a valid unavailable response from a host mapping limit, and implement only the observed bounded allocation contract. Preserve backing coherence between DosHost GuestMemory and Unicorn, and do not make an unbounded 32-bit arena.
acceptance: Evidence identifies original-byte AX=0501 request size, EIP, return registers, and whether failure is due to modeled limit or allocation failure
Unit tests cover AX=0501 allocation success, boundary/failure, handle return, bounds, and no guest-memory corruption
Unicorn maps and coherently backs any successful AX=0501 allocation without overlapping guest/image/PSP/MCB or existing allocations
Original-byte -k trace continues past the first AX=0501 call and records the next exact service/exception/stop; no MENU claim without direct evidence
Existing DPMI AX=0100, AX=0102, AX=0300/INT 2F, and runtime suites remain passing
